h.select_rule: Reject any hypothesis whose condition is the edited field's own value or makes the edit inert, and reject any that restates a main effect. Keep 10 with distinct mechanisms, no repeated condition setting more than twice, both directions, and the most surprising yet mechanistically defensible claims.
h.strategy: Generate widely, then let selection prune. Each hypothesis must couple two different fields: the condition should change HOW the edit works, not whether the edited part is used at all. Draw on the negated default assumptions, for example that a stronger setting is always better, that effects are additive, or that more paths always help. Propose cases of saturation when an equivalent capacity already exists elsewhere, compensation where one part masks another's weakness, and reversals where a usually beneficial edit hurts under a specific configuration. Do not explain a hypothesis by saying an edit is inert, or by saying that upgrading a weak setting helps more than upgrading a strong one. In each 'why', state the mechanism concisely and say what observation would refute it.

hyps.why: A deep 3-conv chain (0-1-2-3) benefits from an identity shortcut that eases optimization; refuted if the skip gain is no larger when edge 2 is conv_3x3 than otherwise.
With an identity route already present, a 1x1 on 1->3 adds redundant channel mixing without new spatial context; refuted if the 1x1 gain is equal or larger under a direct skip.
Skip into node 2 hands the raw input to a 3x3 on 2->3, giving a clean single-conv path; refuted if the gain is no larger than with other edge-1 ops.
Pooling after a conv forms a conv-pool block that smooths and regularizes learned features; refuted if pooling on edge 2 is no better after conv than after skip.
Skip merges node 1 into a node already fed by a 3x3, mixing two feature levels redundantly; refuted if the effect is the same or better with conv on edge 1.
A conv feeding a pool on the 2->3 edge completes a conv-then-pool pipeline, so conv on edge 1 is more useful than when edge 5 is something else; refuted if no difference.
An alternative shortcut via node 2 compensates for the lost direct route; refuted if removal is equally harmful.
Skip into node 1 makes edge 4 a duplicate of a direct conv path from the input, so it adds redundancy instead of depth; refuted if no loss relative to other edge-4 ops.
Identity at both 0->3 and 2->3 yields a dominance of identity terms in the output sum, diluting learned features; refuted if the effect is unchanged.
A pooled node 1 has lost sharp features, and a 3x3 on edge 2 recovers feature extraction; refuted if the conv gain is no larger after pool than after conv.
